title: Testing with node:test
summary: Write tests with node:test and assert, run them with node --test, and fix a function until they pass.

quiz.q: What is the main benefit of an automated test?
options: It makes the program run faster
It checks your code in seconds every time you change it, so mistakes show up early
It writes the code for you
It removes the need for functions
quiz.explain: Tests are small programs that call your code and compare the result with what you expect. Run them after every change and you notice breakage immediately.

quiz.q: Complete the command that runs all tests with the built-in test runner.
quiz.explain: `node --test` finds test files such as `*.test.js` (and any file inside a `test` folder) and runs them. No extra package is needed.

quiz.q: Put the steps of fixing a bug with a test in the best order.
lines: Write a test that describes the correct behaviour
Run node --test and see the test fail
Run node --test again and see the test pass
quiz.explain: A test that has never failed might not be testing anything. Seeing it fail first proves it catches the bug, and seeing it pass afterwards proves your change fixed it.

quiz.q: What happens when an assert call such as assert.equal(1 + 1, 3) fails?
options: It prints a warning and carries on
It throws an AssertionError, and the test is marked as failed
Nothing, asserts only work in browsers
quiz.explain: A failed assertion throws an error. The test runner catches it, reports which test failed and shows the expected and actual values.

quiz.q: A function should give an 'A' for marks of 75 and above. Which marks are the most useful extra test cases?
options: 74 and 75, the values on each side of the boundary
quiz.explain: Bugs often hide at boundaries, for example `>` written instead of `>=`. Testing the value just below and exactly on the limit catches them.

exercise.task:
`grades.js` has a function `gradeFor(mark)` that is supposed to turn a mark out of 100 into a letter. A set of tests (like the ones you would run with `node --test`) shows it is wrong. Fix it so it behaves like this:

- 75 and above: `'A'`
- 60 to 74: `'B'`
- 40 to 59: `'C'`
- below 40: `'F'`
- A mark below 0, above 100 or not a number must throw a `RangeError` with the message `Mark must be between 0 and 100`.

Keep `module.exports = { gradeFor };`.
hints: Run the examples in your head: which boundary marks (75, 60, 40) does the current code treat wrongly?
Boundaries need `>=` (greater than or equal to), not `>`. Validate the input first: if the mark is not a number or is outside 0 to 100, throw before you grade.
